units.oneLiner: Keep every key in the slot array itself and, when the home slot is taken, probe the next slot and the next: the probes stay inside the cache line the first one fetched, Knuth's 1963 formulas say exactly what each load factor costs, and the price is clustering, which is why the table resizes before it is full and why the hash must scatter neighbors.
units.description: Linear probing on 65,536 slots against Knuth's 1963 formulas (within 1% to load 0.7) and a Python set over 1,200,000 operations: at load 0.9 a hit costs 5.315 probes but 1.540 cache lines against 2.570 and 2.570 for double hashing; clusters of 715 slots; tombstones 5.864 probes per miss against 1.698 for backward shift; a weak hash costs 1,056 probes per hit.
units.time: O(1) expected; (1 + 1/(1 - a)) / 2 probes per hit

narration_plan.release: not generated yet (generate right before publication)

units.plan_row: Open addressing × Linear probing. Puzzle 172, data-structures (problemSlug hash-collision-resolution, the atlas problem page carrying "Cache-friendly hashing"; sibling live lesson cuckoo-hashing-two-table-eviction-kicks). Solution open_addressing_linear_probing.py (3.0s, prints OK): linear probing with tombstone or backward-shift deletion and a rebuild at 85% live-plus-tombstones, quadratic probing (triangular offsets), double hashing (odd stride), separate chaining, Robin Hood, Fibonacci and weak hashes, a probe-and-cache-line counter (8 slots per 64-byte line, one line per chaining node). ORACLES: (1) Knuth 1963 at loads 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95: hits 1.164 / 1.509 / 2.172 / 3.027 / 5.962 / 11.609 against 1.167 / 1.500 / 2.167 / 3.000 / 5.500 / 10.500, misses 1.397 / 2.510 / 5.971 / 12.655 / 50.434 / 205.639 against 1.389 / 2.500 / 6.056 / 13.000 / 50.500 / 200.500 (within 6% to 0.8, 20% beyond); (2) 1,200,000 mixed operations across six structures all matching a Python set, final sizes matching; (3) the race at load 0.9 (every key looked up, 5,000 misses): linear probing 5.315 probes/hit, 47.975/miss, 1.540 lines/hit, variance 277, max 612, longest cluster 715; Robin Hood 5.315 / 5.644 / 1.540 / 19.8 / 29; quadratic 2.850 / 12.055 / 1.951 / 16.2 / 92; double hashing 2.570 / 10.056 / 2.570 / 11.1 / 68; chaining 2.450 / 1.923 / 2.450 / 0.5 / 9; longest run by load 8 / 31 / 85 / 209 / 752 / 3,250; (4) deletion: fill to 0.7, delete half: tombstones 5.864 probes per miss (formula for 0.7: 6.056), backward shift 1.698 (formula for 0.35: 1.683); (5) weak hash (high bits) on 2,048 consecutive keys in 4,096 slots: linear probing 1,056 probes per hit, double hashing 8.3, chaining 402.8, strong hash 1.50. Honest: linear probing pays twice double hashing's probes at 0.9 and wins only on lines; the Robin Hood mean is identical to 1e-9 (the displacement total is invariant), asserted; three author notes recorded (quadratic vs double ordering; the first weak-hash experiment at 65,536 slots ran quadratic for ten minutes and was shrunk; a 5,000-key hit sample was replaced by every key after the early-inserted keys biased it). Cards: self, Hash table with chaining, Robin Hood hashing, Cuckoo hashing (live lesson badge) (all algoName). neverUse: linear probing with a hash that keeps neighbors neighbors. Figure: Knuth's hit and miss curves with the measured points beside bars of the longest run by load; cite Knuth 1963 / TAOCP 3 6.4, Amdahl et al. 1954, Pagh-Pagh-Ruzic STOC 2007 DOI 10.1145/1250790.1250839. Viz LinearProbingViz: a 64-slot table as eight cache lines filling to load 0.9, walked slots amber and touched lines outlined, the running average probes per insert against Knuth's expectation, every key checked reachable from its home each tick; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 21 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 500, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba.

units.oneLiner: Seal the bids, give the item to the highest, and charge the second bid: your bid then decides only whether you win, never what you pay, so the truth is a dominant strategy, the highest value always wins, and the seller earns exactly what a first-price auction would at equilibrium, without anyone computing one.
units.description: The Vickrey auction against exhaustive deviation checks and closed forms: 0 profitable deviations in 4,029,261 comparisons; the highest value wins 60,000 of 60,000 draws; revenue 0.4997 at n = 3 against first-price 0.4994 and theory 0.5; Myerson's reserve 0.5 lifts two-bidder revenue from 0.333 to 0.418; a seller shill steals 0.2496 per sale.
units.time: O(n log n) to sort the bids, O(n) with two running maxima
units.plan_row: Vickrey auction × Second-price rule. Puzzle 189, optimization-or (problemSlug auction-design, the atlas problem page carrying "Truthful single-item auction"; sibling live lessons gale-shapley-deferred-acceptance, puzzle 73, and secretary-one-over-e). Solution vickrey_auction_second_price_rule.py (0.76s, prints OK): a Vickrey auction with optional reserve, a first-price auction, an ascending clock auction, second-price and first-price payoff functions, the expected first-price payoff against equilibrium rivals, the closed-form two-bidder reserve revenue 1/3 + r^2 - 4r^3/3, and a mean with standard error. ORACLES, i.i.d. uniform [0, 1] values, 60,000 draws per cell: (1) dominant strategy exhaustively: 21 values x 21 highest rival bids x 21 deviations = 9,261 grid comparisons plus 20,000 random continuous profiles x 201 deviations = 4,020,000, total 4,029,261 comparisons, 0 profitable deviations from the truth; under a first-price rule 210 of the 441 grid (value, rival) cells reward shading; (2) first-price equilibrium by best response: against rivals bidding (n - 1)v/n, the best reply on a 1,000-bid grid is within 0.0007 of (n - 1)v/n over n = 2, 3, 5 and v = 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, and bidding v earns exactly 0 (equilibrium utility 0.149 on average); (3) revenue equivalence: Vickrey 0.3351 +/- 0.0010, 0.4997 +/- 0.0009, 0.6665 +/- 0.0007 at n = 2, 3, 5 against first-price at equilibrium 0.3340 +/- 0.0005, 0.4994 +/- 0.0005, 0.6668 +/- 0.0005 and theory (n - 1)/(n + 1) = 0.3333, 0.5, 0.6667, all within three standard errors; the highest value won 60,000 of 60,000 at every n; an ascending clock at increment 0.001 matched the Vickrey winner on 3,000 of 3,000 draws and the price within 0.001, 500 rounds per auction on average; (4) Myerson's reserve: the closed form peaks at r = 0.500 on a 1,000-point grid; simulated two-bidder revenue 0.3330 +/- 0.0010 (r = 0, formula 0.3333), 0.3859 +/- 0.0008 (0.3, formula 0.3873), 0.4181 +/- 0.0010 (0.5, formula 0.4167), 0.3674 +/- 0.0015 (0.7, formula 0.3660), each within three standard errors, 0.5 the best; unsold 0%, 9.2%, 24.7%, 48.8%; (5) efficiency and the negative example: Vickrey misallocates on 0 of 60,000 draws; a first-price auction between a bidder shading by half and one shading by a fifth misallocates 18.7% of draws and loses 3.5% of welfare; a seller who reads the bids and shills just under the winner extracts 0.2496 +/- 0.0008 per sale at n = 3, the whole gap E[v1 - v2] = 1/(n + 1) = 0.25. Author correction recorded (the draft called the two-bidder reserve gain a third; the formula gives 1/3 to 5/12, a quarter). Cards: self, VCG mechanism, Myerson optimal auction, Ascending clock auction (all algoName; pages verified in dist/algo). neverUse: the second-price rule with a seller who can read the bids (the shill) or colluding bidders. Figure: payoff against bid for a bidder with value 0.8 facing a rival bid of 0.5 under both rules (the second-price step, flat above the rival, truth optimal; first-price 0.8 - b, truth earns 0) beside the two-bidder revenue curve against the reserve with four measured points peaking at 0.5; cite Vickrey 1961 Journal of Finance DOI 10.1111/j.1540-6261.1961.tb02789.x, Myerson 1981, Clarke 1971, Groves 1973. Viz VickreyViz: sixty three-bidder sealed-bid auctions, one per tick, bars for the bids with the winner green and the amber second-price line, a probed bidder's payoff-against-bid step curve, running Vickrey and equilibrium first-price revenue against (n - 1)/(n + 1) = 0.5; invariant every tick: the highest value wins, pays the second value, and 41 probed deviations never beat the truth; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 60 ticks, 0 breaks (2,460 deviations per cycle); stepMs 420, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba, plan 24,648 billable characters, $0.739440, approval c7655390b9358213981744154c7a73362d200ca998287d362890a6b3d61a6688 (not generated yet). units.oneLiner: Scan the pixels once in reading order, giving each foreground pixel the label of a neighbor already seen or a fresh one, record every meeting of two labels as a union, then rewrite each label to its root in a second pass: two streaming reads, no stack, no recursion, and a merge-only table sized by labels, not pixels.
units.description: Two-pass labeling against a flood-fill referee: equal partitions on 88 image-connectivity pairs; 38,400 visits (two per pixel) against 41,280 and 63,360; 179 and 78 provisional labels for 28 and 27 blobs merged by 151 and 51 unions at 0.635 and 0.405 links per find; a 3,220-pixel snake crashes a recursive fill; the naive single pass splits every U.
units.time: O(n α(n)): two passes over n pixels, near-constant per union and find
units.space: O(L) parent and rank entries for L provisional labels, plus the label image
units.baseline: Breadth-first flood fill from every unlabeled pixel
units.plan_row: Connected component labeling × Two-pass union-find. Puzzle 190, signal-graphics (problemSlug region-labeling, the atlas problem page carrying "Region labeling"; sibling live lessons canny-edge-detector-hysteresis-thresholding, puzzle 173, and unionfind-rank-compression, puzzle 8). Solution connected_component_labeling_two_pass_union_find.py (0.3s, prints OK): a counting union-find (unions, finds, parent links followed) with path compression and union by rank, the two-pass labeler (visits, provisional labels), an iterative BFS flood fill (visits, queue maximum), a recursive flood fill (max depth, RecursionError reported instead of crashing), run-length labeling, union-find over raw pixels, the naive single pass, and image builders (random disks, separated disks, a one-pixel-wide snake, U shapes, diagonal stripes). ORACLES: (1) partition equality (never label numbers) against the BFS on a 160 x 120 image of 60 disks (5,520 foreground pixels) under 4- and 8-connectivity, on 40 random 64 x 48 images under both (80 pairs), and on 10, 25, and 40 separated disks whose counts are known by construction: 88 comparisons, with run-length labeling and pixel union-find agreeing too; (2) counts: 28 / 27 components; two-pass 38,400 visits (exactly 2 per pixel, asserted) against BFS 41,280 / 63,360 (queue max 30 / 50); provisional labels 179 / 78, unions 151 / 51, finds 7,934 / 7,474 at 0.635 / 0.405 links per find (asserted under 1.5); unions == sets made minus components asserted for every method; run-length 499 runs, 471 / 472 unions, 1,443 / 1,455 finds; pixel union-find 5,520 sets, 5,492 / 5,493 unions, 25,588 / 45,026 finds at 0.824 / 0.889 links; recursive fill 41,280 / 63,360 visits (equal to BFS, asserted), depth 597 / 573; (3) snake 160 x 40 (3,220 pixels, one component): two-pass 12,800 visits, 11 labels, 10 unions; BFS queue max 1; recursive fill depth 3,220 at limit 50,000 and RecursionError at the default 1,000 (asserted); (4) diagonal stripes 60 x 60 period 3: 1,200 components under 4-connectivity (every pixel alone), 39 under 8 (asserted against the stripe count); (5) negative example: naive single pass 60 labels for 30 U shapes (asserted at least 2 per U) and 78 for 27 blobs under 8-connectivity; the two-pass made the same 60 provisional labels and 30 unions on the U image. Honest: author correction recorded (the draft expected about one provisional label per component; measured several per blob, 179 for 28 under 4-connectivity, because every row where a blob widens on its left starts a label). Cards: self, Flood fill, Union-find (live lesson badge, puzzle 8), Run-length encoding (all algoName; pages verified in dist/algo). neverUse: one raster pass with no equivalence table (60 labels for 30 U shapes), with the recursive flood fill crash as its cousin. Figure: pass one on a U shape with labels 1 and 2 and the amber union at the corner, beside a log-scale chart of sets made and finds spent (two-pass 78 / 7,474; run-length 499 / 1,455; pixel union-find 5,520 / 45,026); cite Rosenfeld and Pfaltz JACM 1966 DOI 10.1145/321356.321357, He, Chao, Suzuki IEEE TIP 2008, Wu, Otoo, Suzuki PAA 2009. Viz ComponentLabelingViz: a seeded 48 x 16 image (disks, two U shapes, specks) under 4- or 8-connectivity per cycle; pass one six pixels per tick with provisional-label colors and an amber flash per union, pass two twelve per tick recoloring to final components; invariant every tick of pass one: the union-find classes over the scanned prefix equal an independent flood fill's components of that prefix; at the end partition equality with the full flood fill, visits == 2N, unions == labels minus components; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 191 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 60, holdTicks rests. units.oneLiner: Draw every trial's hyperparameters independently and uniformly (log-uniform across orders of magnitude), train, keep the best: n trials hit the top 5% of the space with probability 1 - 0.95^n in any dimension, and because only a few knobs matter, n random trials try n values of the one that does where a grid of the same size tries k.
units.description: Random search against the 1 - 0.95^n theorem (0.954 measured at 60 trials), grids, and Latin hypercubes: a k x k grid tries k values of the knob that matters, reaching 0.35, 0.92, 0.40 of the optimum at k = 3, 4, 5; a 15,625-point six-knob grid 0.41 against 0.96 for 60 random trials; a ridge learner within 5% of optimum in 91% and 99% of repeats.
units.plan_row: Random search × Uniform hyperparameter sampling. Puzzle 192, ml-ai (problemSlug hyperparameter-tuning, the atlas problem page carrying "Hyperparameter tuning"; topic model-selection, tier 1; sibling live lessons hill-climbing-random-restarts, puzzle 178, and annealing-cooling, puzzle 2). Solution random_search_uniform_hyperparameter_sampling.py (2.9 s, prints OK, deterministic across runs): uniform, full-factorial grid, and Latin hypercube samplers; a two-dimensional objective with one important axis (peak of width 0.12 at x = 0.37, weak y) and its six-dimensional extension; a top-5%-by-volume threshold (400 x 400 grid in 2-D, 200,000 samples in 6-D) with hit probabilities and standard errors; a Chebyshev-feature polynomial ridge learner (14 training, 200 validation points; knobs degree 1-10, lambda 1e-7 to 1e2 log scale, and one knob the closed-form solver ignores) with a Gaussian-elimination solver; and a closed-form gradient-descent loss on curvatures 1 to 100. ORACLES: (1) THEOREM: P(top 5% hit by n draws) = 0.4080 +/- 0.0049, 0.7793 +/- 0.0041, 0.9539 +/- 0.0021 at n = 10, 30, 60 over 10,000 repeats against 1 - 0.95^n = 0.4013, 0.7854, 0.9539 (each within 3 SE); (2) LOW EFFECTIVE DIMENSIONALITY, 300 repeats: k x k grid = exactly k distinct x values, best/optimum 0.349, 0.916, 0.404, 0.944, 0.916, 0.802 at k = 3..8 (falls 4 to 5 and 7 to 8: alignment lottery, asserted); k^2 random trials = k^2 distinct x, 0.768 +/- 0.014, 0.884, 0.919, 0.950, 0.967, 0.972 +/- 0.001 (rises, beats the grid by > 0.2 at k = 3 and 5, asserted); Latin hypercube 0.885, 0.926, 0.955, 0.966, 0.969, 0.976; (3) LEARNER: dense scan of 3,610 settings, optimum validation MSE 0.0521 at degree 3, lambda 0.0596; within-5% region = 8.5% of the space, so the theorem predicts hit rates 0.91 (27) and 1.00 (64); measured over 200 repeats: random 0.91 and 0.99 (mean best/opt 1.033 +/- 0.009, 1.004 +/- 0.001), LHS 0.98 and 1.00 (1.007 +/- 0.003, 1.002); grid 3 per axis: 9 distinct (degree, lambda) pairs of 27 trainings, 4.915x optimum, miss; grid 4 per axis: 16 of 64, 1.430x, miss (all asserted; random hit rate within 3 SE + 0.03 of 1 - (1 - 0.085)^n; LHS hits at least as often as random); (4) LEARNING RATE on [1e-5, 1], stable below 0.020, best 0.0194 (loss 1.13e-2), 20 draws x 2,000 repeats: uniform converging 0.0195 +/- 0.0007 (theory 0.0200), any convergent draw 0.315, a draw within 2x of the best rate 0.168 (theory 0.187), median best loss/opt 8.5; log-uniform 0.6585 +/- 0.0024 (theory 0.6602), 1.000, 0.721 (theory 0.728), 3.9 (all four closed forms asserted within 3 SE); (5) NEGATIVE EXAMPLE: 5^6 = 15,625-training grid, 5 distinct values per knob, best 0.415 of the six-knob optimum; 60 random trainings 0.963 +/- 0.001 (above 0.9 in 97% of 500 repeats), top-5% hit probability 0.956 +/- 0.003 (theory 0.9539). Two author corrections recorded in the header: the loss-window criterion (0.07 vs 0.27, exponentially sensitive loss) replaced by the rate window; the 40-point draft learner (everything hit the 5% band) replaced by 14 points (band = 8.5% of the space). A measured Gaussian-process expected-improvement rival (95% within 5% at 27, 1.025 +/- 0.020, a draw with random) was authored and then REMOVED to fit the 20 KB page-chunk budget (its GP code alone cost about 1 KB gzipped); the Bayesian optimization card is now qualitative, like Vickrey's VCG card. Cards: self, Grid search, Latin hypercube sampling, Bayesian optimization × Expected improvement (algoName Expected improvement, unmeasured); all algo pages exist. neverUse: an exhaustive grid when six knobs each get five values (15,625 trainings at 0.415 against 60 random at 0.963). Contest: the ridge learner at budgets 27 and 64 (five rows, LHS best at 27). Figure: the Bergstra-Bengio projection picture (4 x 4 grid vs 16 random points, the peak band in green, ticks on the x axis showing 4 against 16 distinct values; the 1 - 0.95^n curve panel was dropped for the chunk budget); cites Bergstra and Bengio JMLR 13 (2012), Li et al. Hyperband JMLR 18 (2018), Snoek, Larochelle, Adams NeurIPS 2012, McKay, Beckman, Conover Technometrics 1979. Viz RandomSearchViz: grid vs random on the same hidden objective, one trial per tick per panel, k seeded 3 to 7, distinct-x counters, best-so-far rings, invariant (equal trial counts, unit square, monotone bests, grid distinct x <= k, end recount equals both bests); NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles, 0 breaks, 30.25 ticks per cycle; stepMs 400, holdTicks rests. units.oneLiner: Cut the address into offset, index, and tag, let the index pick one small set, and compare only that set's W tags in parallel: the direct-mapped cache's one-step lookup with room for W colliding lines, so a few ways erase most conflict misses (2,357 to 381 at four ways on a Zipf trace, 6,144 to 192 on three aligned arrays) while a stride that aims a hundred blocks at one set still needs tiling or full associativity.
units.description: A 16 KB cache at 1 to 256 ways against two independent references (206,976 agreements), 240,000 bit-exact address rebuilds, and Belady's floor: three arrays one cache size apart miss 6,144 of 6,144 direct-mapped and two-way but 192 four-way; a column walk misses 100% below full associativity, 12.5% tiled; Zipf conflicts 2,357, 990, 381, 201, 0.
units.time: O(W) tag compares per access, in parallel: one step
units.space: capacity plus tag, valid, and recency bits (3.71% to 6.84% here)
units.plan_row: Set-associative cache × Index-tag lookup. Puzzle 194, languages-compilers (problemSlug cache-organization, the atlas problem page carrying "Cache organization"; sibling live lesson lru-recency-eviction, puzzle 17, named in the narration; rivals Victim cache and Skewed-associative cache share the d phrase). Solution set_associative_cache_index_tag_lookup.py (0.7 s, prints OK): a set-associative simulator parameterized by capacity, block, ways, and policy (LRU, FIFO, random) that splits each address into tag, index, and offset and compares one set's tags; a dictionary direct-mapped reference; an ordered-dictionary fully associative LRU reference; Belady optimal with a heap of next uses; the three C decomposition; traces: a 64 KB sequential sweep, three 4 KB arrays spaced 16 KB apart over four passes, a 128 x 128 matrix of doubles by rows, by columns, and in 16-row tiles, a Zipf trace (40,000 accesses, 4,096 blocks, s = 1.0, hot blocks scattered), and a five-block cycle in one four-way set. ORACLES: (1) the fields reconstruct every address bit for bit in 240,000 checks, index bits = log2(sets), offset bits = log2(block), tag the rest (18/8/6 direct-mapped, 20/6/6 four-way, 26/0/6 fully associative); (2) the general simulator equals the direct-mapped reference at W = 1 and the fully associative LRU reference at S = 1 on 206,976 decisions over every trace; (3) Belady misses no more than any configuration on any trace; (4) misses = compulsory + capacity + conflict, conflict 0 when fully associative; (5) measured: sweep and row walk 12.5% everywhere (compulsory only); three arrays (192 of 256 blocks fit) direct-mapped 6,144 of 6,144, 2-way 6,144, 4-way 192 (first touches), 32 KB direct-mapped still 67.7%; column walk 100% at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 ways, 12.5% fully associative, 12.5% direct-mapped in 16-row tiles; Zipf miss rates 48.05 / 44.63 / 43.11 / 42.66 / 42.52 / 42.16% at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 256 ways, compulsory 3,535, capacity 13,328, conflict 2,357 / 990 / 381 / 201 / 146 / 0, Belady 10,282 misses (25.70%); rule of thumb direct-mapped 16 KB 19,220 against two-way 8 KB 21,524 (ratio 0.893); replacement at 4 ways on Zipf LRU 17,244, FIFO 18,760, random 18,798; five blocks cycling one four-way set: LRU 10,000 of 10,000, FIFO 10,000, random 4,014, Belady 2,503, four blocks LRU 4; comparators 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 256 per access, tag + valid + LRU overhead 3.71 / 4.10 / 4.49 / 4.88 / 5.27 / 6.84% of data bits. Honest: ways do not fix a stride (said in the weakness and the negative example); LRU loses to random on the five-block cycle. Two author corrections recorded (associativity below full does not rescue the column walk; the three arrays fit three to a set, so four ways miss only first touches, not one in eight). Cards: self, Victim cache, Skewed-associative cache, Loop tiling (all algoName, pages present). neverUse: a direct-mapped cache under streams spaced a cache size apart. Figure: the 32-bit address split for direct-mapped, four-way, and fully associative beside a bar chart of Zipf conflict misses by ways; cite Hill and Smith 1989 DOI 10.1109/12.40842, Smith 1982 DOI 10.1145/356887.356892, Hennessy and Patterson appendix B. Viz SetAssociativeCacheViz: an eight-block cache as 8 x 1, 4 x 2, or 2 x 4 by cycle serving three arrays one cache size apart for two passes (96 accesses), one access per tick, address bits colored by field, the indexed set outlined, hit and miss flashes, counters for hits, misses, and tag compares; invariant: an independent per-set LRU reference agrees on every access and the fields rebuild the address, and at the end direct-mapped and two-way missed everything while four-way missed only the six first touches; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles, 96 ticks each, 0 breaks; stepMs 380, holdTicks rests. units.oneLiner: Count each symbol, divide by n, and plug the frequencies into Shannon's formula: one pass, nothing to tune, and a bias that is always negative and known to first order, (k − 1)/(2n ln 2) bits, so that at ten samples per symbol one added term makes it honest and at one sample per symbol nothing does.
units.description: The plug-in entropy estimator against its exact expectation: bias −0.0728 bits at n = 1,000 for 100 equiprobable symbols (Miller −0.0714), −0.00715 at 10,000, −3.41 at n = 10; Miller-Madow and the jackknife erase it at n ≫ k; a 2,000-symbol tail at n = 2,000 sits 0.583 bits low; independent variables show 0.0587 bits of plug-in mutual information.
units.time: O(n + k) per estimate: one pass over the samples, one over the counts
units.baseline: Compressed size per symbol (Huffman on the counts)
units.plan_row: Shannon entropy estimation × Maximum likelihood plug-in. Puzzle 195, compression-coding (problemSlug entropy-estimation, the atlas problem page carrying "Entropy estimation"; sibling live lesson huffman-frequency-merges). Solution shannon_entropy_estimation_maximum_likelihood_plug_in.py (0.7 s, prints OK, 62 assertions): the plug-in in its log n form, Miller-Madow and jackknife corrections, the EXACT expectation of the plug-in as a sum of binomial terms (a brute force over every count vector on a 4-symbol alphabet at n = 8 agrees to 1e-12: 1.532790 bits against a truth of 1.846439), a Huffman coder on the counts, Zipf distributions, and a plug-in mutual information. ORACLES: (1) 100 equiprobable symbols (6.644 bits): exact bias -3.41 at n = 10 (E[plug-in] 3.233, log2 10 = 3.322), -2.01 at 30, -0.822 at 100 (Miller first-order -0.714), -0.261 at 300, -0.0728 at 1,000 (-0.0714), -0.0239 at 3,000, -0.00715 at 10,000 (-0.00714); Miller-Madow -2.79, -1.40, -0.370, -0.034, -0.0012 (exact -0.00136), -0.0001, -0.0000; jackknife -2.12, -0.83, -0.065, +0.027, +0.0018, +0.0002, -0.0000; sd 0.0101 at 1,000 and 0.0009 at 10,000 (ratio 11.06: the uniform leading variance term vanishes, 1/n). (2) Zipf over 100 symbols (5.310 bits): bias -2.43 at n = 10, -0.663 at 100, -0.0765 at 1,000 (sd 0.0738), -0.0072 at 10,000 (sd 0.0217; ratio 3.40 against root ten 3.16); Miller-Madow -0.0104 and jackknife +0.0031 at 1,000.
